validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed, not a phantom. PNGRB's own regulator register (NGPL MIS Report, 31-May-2026 edition, under_construction section Sr.No.5) shows physical progress against the authorisation -- 59 km hydrotested, 132 km welded, 113 km lowered out of 160 km authorised, entity GAIL, authorised 12.07.2023, target Jul-26 -- plus independent contemporaneous press: Oil & Gas Journal (23-Jun-2023, 'GAIL wins Gurdaspur-Jammu gas pipeline project'), Business Standard (Jun-2023 award), Kashmir Observer (05-Dec-2024, work commenced, quoting Union Minister Jitendra Singh), CGDIndia (May-2024, GAIL's own tender notice), and IBTimes India (14-Jun-2026, ~90% complete). This is a real, actively-progressing pipeline. CLASSIFICATION: correct -- PNGRB-authorised common-carrier transmission trunk, matches the regulator's own category. DUPLICATE: checked against all 9 roster rows. P3913 Bhatinda-Gurdaspur Gas Pipeline is NOT the same pipe -- the register lists it as a SEPARATE authorisation (Sr.No.2, partially_commissioned, entity GIGL, authorised 261 km / 42.4 MMSCMD, Punjab only) held by a different entity than Gurdaspur-Jammu (Sr.No.5, GAIL, 160 km / 3.10 MMSCMD, Punjab+J&K). The two form a legitimate sequential chain (Bhatinda->Gurdaspur feeds into Gurdaspur->Jammu), not a double-count of one line. ATTRIBUTION: route (Gurdaspur, Punjab -> Jammu, J&K via Pathankot/Kathua/Samba) confirmed by every source found -- correct, see Location fill below; Owner/Operator were BLANK on the operators/owners tab and are filled below (GAIL, 100%, confirmed by the register + OGJ). SPEC -- the real finding: GEM's current Capacity (2.00 MMSCMD) and LengthKnown (175.00 km) do NOT match the pipeline's current, regulator-of-record specification, and neither cell carries a ref (both were MISSING_REF). Two independent, current, mutually-agreeing sources give Capacity = 3.10 MMSCMD (+0.775 MMSCMD reserve): the PNGRB MIS register (authorised_capacity_mmscmd=3.1, determined_capacity_mmscmd=3.1) AND CGDIndia's report of GAIL's own May-2024 tender notice ('system capacity of 3.10 million standard cubic meters a day (mmscmd) with extra capacity of 0.775 mmscmd'). For length, the register's authorised_length_km=160.0 is independently matched by Union Minister Jitendra Singh's own on-the-record statement quoted inside the sheet's ALREADY-CITED Kashmir Observer article ('The 160-km Gurdaspur-Jammu Tawi natural gas pipeline project has started...') -- two independent sources at 160 km. A third current source, GAIL's own May-2024 tender notice (CGDIndia), gives a close but not identical 152 km (mainline chainage Ch 76.735-151.35, i.e. the engineered pipe length excluding some approach/tie-in allowance folded into the register's rounder 160 km). All three current sources (160, 160, 152) sit well below GEM's 175 km. GEM's 175 km / 2.00 MMSCMD pair traces to the original 2023 award reporting -- Oil & Gas Journal's 23-Jun-2023 piece states exactly '2-million standard cu m/day' and '175 kilometers', and this looks like the actual origin of the sheet's current numbers. The 175-km figure is also the SAME Kashmir Observer article's own headline/lede ('the 175-km Gurdaspur-Jammu Tawi natural gas pipeline project'), which the SAME article self-contradicts three sentences later by quoting the Minister's 160-km figure -- i.e. even the sheet's own currently-cited source disagrees with itself, and the 175 number is the one NOT corroborated by the regulator. Best explanation: 175 km/2.0 MMSCMD were the pre-tender bid-stage estimates (2.0 MMSCMD closely matches the 'minimum system capacity of at least 2.0 MMSCMD' bid-qualification threshold that PNGRB used for the downstream Jammu-Srinagar extension, per The Week, 02-Feb-2024 -- a plausible source of the figure's origin), later superseded by GAIL's detailed-engineering tender spec (152-160 km / 3.10 MMSCMD) that the current PNGRB register also reflects. This is a stale-figure defect, not a unit error -- flagging as a material spec disagreement per standing rule, not silently passing it.
